title: axe select-name: six filter <select> elements have no accessible name
description: axe-core rule `select-name` (impact: critical), 6 instances across 4 tabs at runtime. Screen-reader users hear only "combo box" with no indication of what each filter does. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species filter), :872 (county filter), :896 (media filter); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604 (county filter); LifeList.tsx:616 (county filter, the Multimedia tab); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376 (county filter). The visual label is a decorative MapPin icon with pointerEvents:'none', so nothing names the control. Checklists.tsx:629/:644 does this correctly with aria-label="Protocol"/"County" — that tab had zero select-name violations, proving the in-house fix pattern.
fix: Add aria-label to each select, matching the Checklists.tsx pattern: aria-label="Species filter" / "County" / "Media type" on the MapExplorer selects, and aria-label="County" on the SpeciesDetail, LifeList, and BreedingCodeList county selects.

title: axe label: From/To date inputs on three tabs have no accessible name
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions A)
description: axe-core rule `label` (impact: critical), 6 instances across 3 tabs at runtime. The date-range filter inputs are announced as unlabeled date fields, and the only visual relationship cue is a decorative Calendar icon and a "→" span. Locations: SpeciesDetail.tsx:630 and :644, LifeList.tsx:645 and :659 (Multimedia tab), BreedingCodeList.tsx:409 and :425. The identical control in Checklists.tsx:655/:663 carries aria-label="From date"/"To date" and passed — the fix pattern already exists in the codebase.
fix: Copy the Checklists.tsx pattern: add aria-label="From date" / aria-label="To date" to both date inputs in SpeciesDetail.tsx, LifeList.tsx, and BreedingCodeList.tsx.

title: Species Detail / Named Birds map pins (DOM markers) have no keyboard access path
description: The shared SightingsMap renders each sighting pin as a react-map-gl <Marker> whose content is a plain <div> with a click handler routed through Marker onClick — no tabIndex, no role, no keydown handler — so a keyboard user can never open the per-coordinate popup. On Species Detail ("Sighting Locations" map) that popup is the ONLY place exposing the per-sighting checklist links for sightings without comments (Top Locations rows at SpeciesDetail.tsx:1122-1137 show only name+count; the Comments section only covers commented sightings), so those eBird links are pointer-only functionality. Same pattern, lower impact (keyboard equivalents exist nearby): TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 chip markers (mitigated by the sidebar "Nearest Targets" locate buttons opening the same popup) and BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 geographic-stats rank pins (popup content fully duplicated in the adjacent "Top locations" text lists). Named Birds card maps are also unreachable but each row already lists every sighting's checklist link (NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100). Note ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim covers only the Map Explorer GL markers; these DOM-marker maps have no equivalent of its in-view lists.
fix: DOM markers CAN be focusable (unlike the GL pins): make the marker content a <button aria-label={locName + ' — N sightings'}> so Tab+Enter opens the popup, or reuse the Map Explorer pattern (a focusable list of coordinates that drives the same selectedCoord state). For Species Detail specifically, alternatively surface the per-coordinate checklist links in the keyboard-reachable Top Locations rows.

title: Settings tab reorder is drag-and-drop only — no keyboard alternative
description: Tab Layout rows are reordered exclusively via HTML5 drag-and-drop on the <li draggable> (onDragStart/onDragOver/onDrop, Settings.tsx:712-717). The drag handle is a non-focusable <div aria-label="Drag to reorder…"> (line 721-723) — it isn't even in the tab order, and there are no move-up/move-down buttons. The component self-documents the failure with an sr-only note at line 699 ("Keyboard reordering is not supported in this version"), which is honest disclosure but still a WCAG 2.1.1 failure: the reorder function is entirely unavailable to keyboard (and screen-reader) users. The per-row show/hide eye toggles ARE proper buttons, so only ordering is blocked.
fix: Add visible Move up / Move down buttons per row (simplest, also helps touch+AT), or implement the APG keyboard drag pattern (focusable handle, Space to grab, arrows to move, Space to drop, with an aria-live announcement). Then delete the sr-only disclaimer.

title: Mobile filter sidebar: Escape focus-restore is dead code, trap snapshot goes stale, other close paths drop focus — published a11y claim is false
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (and 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap A integrity)
description: Three defects in the one focus trap the app ships: (1) The Escape handler runs `setSidebarOpen(false); filtersButtonRef.current?.focus()` (lines 200-203), but the Filters button is inside the FAB cluster rendered only when the sidebar is CLOSED (`{!sidebarOpen && (<div className="sr-map-fab-cluster">` at line 1446, ref at 1461). While the sidebar is open the ref is null, so the restore is a no-op; the focused element then gets display:none (`.sr-map-sidebar-hidden`) and the browser dumps focus to <body> — the keyboard user restarts from the top of the document. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 51 explicitly claims 'Escape closes it and returns focus to the button that opened it' — that claim is currently false. (2) The focusable list is snapshotted once at open (lines 192-196: `sidebar.querySelectorAll(...)`, then `first`/`last` captured); the sidebar contains a Filters accordion and async-loaded hotspot/target lists, so after content changes Tab escapes the trap into obscured background content (the page behind is not inert). (3) The mobile 'Close filters' button (line 1414) and the backdrop click (line 1400) close via `setSidebarOpen(false)` with no focus restore — same display:none → body drop.
fix: Keep the FAB cluster mounted while the sidebar is open (hide it with CSS/inert) so the ref survives, or restore focus in an effect that runs after sidebarOpen flips to false. Re-query focusables on each Tab keydown (HelpDocs.tsx:258-273 already does this correctly — reuse that pattern). Route ALL close paths (Escape, Close button, backdrop) through one close() that restores focus.

title: Filter selects and date inputs have no accessible name on four tabs
description: The county <select> and the From/To <input type="date"> controls have no aria-label, no <label>, and no title — a screen reader announces an unnamed combo box / date field. Same defect repeats: LifeList.tsx:616 (select), :645, :659 (dates); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376 (select), :409, :425 (dates); MapExplorer.tsx:853 (Species select), :872 (County select), :896 (Media select) — the visual SidebarLabel is a styled <div> with no htmlFor association — and MapExplorer.tsx:862/:864 (two date text inputs distinguished only by placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD"). Checklists.tsx:629/:644/:655/:663 does this correctly (aria-label on each), proving the intended pattern exists in-repo.
fix: Add aria-label to each control matching the Checklists tab pattern (aria-label="County", "From date", "To date", "Species", "Media"), or convert SidebarLabel to a <label htmlFor> association in MapExplorer.

title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). The same style-only-state defect appears in SpeciesDetail.tsx:1189 (Pins/Heatmap map-mode buttons), BirdingStats.tsx:541 (accumulation granularity), :1628 (breeding filter pills), :1717 (media view mode), ListComparer.tsx:215 (My List / Upload source buttons), and MapExplorer.tsx:1030 (hotspot kind-legend toggles, whose only state cue is opacity 0.4). A screen-reader user cannot tell which option is active. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md: "Filter pills announce whether they are pressed." The codebase already has the correct pattern (SortSeg in Checklists.tsx:74, SnowMap.tsx:144, SpeciesDetail graph groups :962/:974).
fix: Add aria-pressed={value === opt.value} (or role="radio"/aria-checked inside a role="radiogroup") to SegControl's buttons and to each listed location; wrap each group in role="group" with an aria-label.

title: Dark theme: white chip/badge text on lightened recency-tier fills fails badly (1.52–1.92:1)
description: tierColors() hardcodes text:'white' for the fresh and mid recency tiers, but the dark-theme tokens lighten those fills (--sr-map-target-fresh #34D399, --sr-map-target-mid #6EE7B7). Computed: white on #34D399 = 1.92:1, white on #6EE7B7 = 1.52:1 (dark); even light-theme mid (#5EA07C) is only 3.09:1. These colors carry the species-name label on every Media Targets map chip (TargetMarkers.tsx:72, 11px/600) and the '≤7 days' tier badge in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:100, 10px/600) — the primary content of the Map Explorer's Media Targets mode is near-unreadable in dark mode. The 'old' tier already does this right (--sr-map-target-old-text adapts per theme, 4.86:1 light / 10.83:1 dark).
fix: Add per-tier text tokens like the existing --sr-map-target-old-text (e.g. --sr-map-target-fresh-text / -mid-text: white in light where the fill is dark enough, dark green like #052E16 in dark where the fills are pastel) and return them from tierColors() instead of the literal 'white'.

title: Breeding-tier colored text on 8–15% tier tints fails in both themes (1.97–4.12:1)
description: Active breeding pills set color: var(--sr-tier-N) over rgba(var(--sr-tier-N-rgb), 0.08–0.15) composited on the card surface. Computed over --sr-surface: LIGHT — tier-1 text on tier-1@0.15 = 2.32:1 (any active tier-1 code pill, and the 'Possible' filter pill in BirdingStats); DARK — tier-4 text 1.97:1 (the active 'Confirmed' category pill), tier-3 text 2.94:1, tier-2 text 4.12:1, tier-2-on-tier-1-tint 3.53:1. Same defect at BreedingCodeList.tsx:58-60 (category pills), SpeciesDetail.tsx:786-788 (breeding category pill), BirdingStats.tsx:1637-1638 (Confirmed/Probable/Possible filter pills). Related same-root-cause case: the white badge count on the tier-2 circle (BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219) is 3.96:1 in dark (tier-2 lightened to #A855F7) while passing in light (5.38:1).
fix: Introduce --sr-tier-N-fg tokens per theme for text-on-tint (dark theme needs the text far lighter than the fill tokens; light theme tier-1 needs the existing --sr-tier-1-text dark purple), and extend the tier-1-text pattern to the dark-mode tier-2 badge circle (dark text on #A855F7 would pass).

title: --sr-text-disabled used for real content text (2.29–2.56:1)
description: The disabled-text token (#A1A1AA light = 2.56:1 on surface, 2.45:1 on bg; #52525B dark = 2.29:1 on surface, 1.93:1 on surface-subtle) is widely used for meaningful, non-disabled content: Settings file sublabels (Settings.tsx:240) and full explanatory paragraphs (Settings.tsx:1143, 1174), file dates (:235), tab-layout 'HIDDEN' labels (:739), Species Detail counters and zero values (SpeciesDetail.tsx:461, 584, 690, 830, 926), comparer '—' and italic placeholders that convey 'no value' (ChecklistComparer.tsx:100, 534), the List Comparer section label (ListComparer.tsx:203), and the LifeList 'no filter' chip (LifeList.tsx:606). The WCAG inactive-control exemption does not apply to any of these — they are informative text.
fix: Replace --sr-text-disabled with --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark on surface) everywhere the text is content rather than a label inside a genuinely disabled control; reserve the disabled token for disabled buttons/inputs only.

title: Filter form controls have no programmatic label across most data tabs
wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (also 2.4.6) AA
description: The county <select> and From/To date inputs are repeated across tabs with no aria-label, no <label for>, and no association to any visible text — a screen-reader user hears an unnamed combobox and two unnamed, indistinguishable date fields. Locations: LifeList.tsx:616 (county select), :644 and :658 (date from/to); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376, :408, :424 (same trio); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604, :629, :643 (same trio). Related instances where a VISIBLE label exists but is not programmatically associated: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species select), :872 (county select), :896 (media select) and :862/:864 (date text inputs) — their 'Species'/'County'/'Media'/'Date Range' headings are SidebarLabel <div>s (map/MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43), so the selects have no accessible name and the two free-text date inputs are distinguishable only by the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (format instruction also vanishes once filled — 3.3.2); Settings.tsx:1214, :1226, :1238 (Latitude/Longitude/Radius number inputs whose labels are plain <div>s at :1213/:1225/:1237); ChecklistComparer.tsx:350-353 ('Checklist A/B' <label> elements with no htmlFor, so the inputs' name falls back to the example-URL placeholder). Checklists.tsx:629-663 does this correctly (aria-label="Protocol"/"County"/"From date"/"To date"), proving the house pattern exists.
fix: Match the Checklists.tsx pattern: add aria-label ("County", "From date", "To date") to the bare selects/date inputs in LifeList, BreedingCodeList, SpeciesDetail. In MapExplorer, render SidebarLabel as a <label htmlFor> (or add aria-label to each control), and give the two date inputs distinct names ("Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)"). In Settings, convert the Latitude/Longitude/Radius caption <div>s to <label htmlFor> with input ids. In ChecklistComparer, add htmlFor/id to the existing <label> elements.

title: Inline error messages are silent to assistive tech (no role=alert/aria-live, no aria-describedby)
description:
Several async form-submission error paths render a plain styled
//

, so a screen-reader user who activates the control hears nothing and must hunt the page to discover the failure. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:105 (place-name search failure), :687 (geolocation error), :1006-1011 (Find Hotspots error), :1227-1232 (Find Recent Sightings error); Settings.tsx:300-309 (malformed/failed CSV upload error in FileRow), :476-485 (API-key save error in KeyRow), :1210 (map-location detect error), :1281-1283 (map defaults save error — additionally the text 'Check your values and try again.' does not identify which of the three fields is invalid); ListComparer.tsx:276-280 (my-list load error). None are associated to their input via aria-describedby either. The codebase has correct reference implementations: App.tsx:668+717-736 (role=alert plus aria-describedby on the input), ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, DropZone.tsx:132, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:184.
fix: Give each error container role="alert" (or aria-live="polite" for non-urgent ones), and where the error relates to a specific input add id + aria-describedby on that input (the App.tsx checklist-input pattern). Make the map-defaults message name the offending field, e.g. "Latitude must be between -90 and 90."

title: Media Targets keyboard path is partial and ACCESSIBILITY.md overstates it
description: Media Target chips are DOM <Marker>s with a click-only <div> (no tabindex/role), so the chips themselves are not operable by keyboard. The only keyboard route to a target popup is the 'Nearest Targets' list (MapExplorer.tsx:1292-1338), which is hard-capped at 10 items sorted by distance from the SEARCH CENTER (nearest10 useMemo, MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) — it is not scoped to the map viewport, does not update on pan/zoom, and shows no over-cap hint. Any target beyond the nearest 10 (easy with a 25-50 mi radius) has no keyboard path at all. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 claims "The Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list works the same way" and that "These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom" — that is true for sightings/hotspots (cap 200, BoundsTracker-driven) but false for targets, so the published statement is currently inaccurate.
fix: Render an InViewMarkerList for targets like the other two modes (items = locationGroups filtered by mapBounds via markersInView, cap 200 with the over-cap hint), keeping 'Nearest Targets' as a convenience list; or at minimum correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center, not viewport-scoped.

title: Help overlay: fixed 200px TOC sidebar never collapses — content column collapses to ~30px at 320px width
description: The HelpDocs body lays the TOC and content side by side with inline styles only — no media query and no wrap. The TOC is `width: 200, flexShrink: 0`, the row adds `padding: '0 24px'` and `gap: 40`, so at a 320 CSS px viewport (e.g. 1280px window at 400% zoom, or a phone) the help content column gets roughly 320 − 48 − 200 − 40 ≈ 32px. Markdown text wraps at one or two characters per line (long words overflow), making the in-app documentation effectively unreadable exactly for the low-vision users most likely to need it. Every other layout in the app handles this (globals.css has a 640px media query; TabNav measures and collapses), so this is the one true reflow failure found. It also contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 ("The layout reflows for narrow windows and at large sizes … without clipping content").
fix: Below a narrow-width breakpoint (~700px), stack the TOC above the content (flexDirection column) or move it behind a disclosure button. A `.sr-help-body` class plus a rule in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css is the smallest change; alternatively reuse the TabNav measurement pattern.

title: Contrast claim is overstated: informational text rendered in the --sr-text-disabled token sits at 2.3–2.6:1 in both themes
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md claims body text and primary interface text meet 4.5:1 in both themes, with exactly one disclosed exception (percentage labels inside chart bars). In fact, real informational text — not disabled controls — is rendered in --sr-text-disabled, which computes to 2.56:1 light (#A1A1AA on #FFFFFF) / 2.45:1 on the page bg, and 2.29:1 dark (#52525B on #18181B). Locations: Checklists.tsx:177 and :668 (the result-count labels that are also the polite live regions), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:100 and NamedBirdsTable.tsx:77 (count labels), SpeciesDetail.tsx:461 ('{n} species' count) and :584 (scientific names inside the species-combobox options), ChecklistComparer.tsx:534 (italic placeholder labels), and the uppercase mini-headers in SetupRequired.tsx:56, ListComparer.tsx:203, HelpDocs.tsx:354. None of these are covered by the statement's disclosed chart-label exception, so the published claim is false as written, and low-vision users genuinely cannot read these labels.
fix: Use --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark — already passing) for all informational text and reserve --sr-text-disabled strictly for genuinely disabled controls; or add a passing 'faint text' token. Then re-verify the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast paragraph.

title: Breeding-code badge contrast fails — in the exact category ACCESSIBILITY.md cites as exemplary (down to 1.71:1 in dark theme)
description: The statement says interface colors meet AA, 'for example, the top breeding-code badge uses dark text on its light tier color.' That is true only for the Breeding Codes table's tier-1 badge (BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219, #3B0764 on #C084FC = 5.68:1 light / 7.31:1 dark). Elsewhere the same badge concept fails: (1) ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge uses `color: var(--sr-on-accent)` on `background: TIER_COLORS[def.tier]` — light theme: white on tier-1 #C084FC = 2.64:1; dark theme: #052E16 on tier-2 #A855F7 = 3.77:1, tier-3 #7C3AED = 2.62:1, tier-4 #6B21A8 = 1.71:1 (the badge text is essentially illegible in dark mode). (2) BreedingCodeTable.tsx:218-219 badge in dark theme: white on tier-2 #A855F7 = 3.96:1 (0.6875rem bold = small text, needs 4.5). (3) SpeciesDetail.tsx:788 breeding pill renders its label in TIER_COLORS[tier]; for tier 1 in light theme that is #C084FC on a near-white 8%-tinted surface ≈ 2.6:1. The published example claim is materially false outside the one table.
fix: In ChecklistComparer, reuse the BreedingCodeTable pattern: per-tier text color (`--sr-tier-1-text` on tier 1, white on tiers 3-4) instead of --sr-on-accent, and add a dark-theme tier-2 text token (white on #A855F7 fails; #1A0030-style dark text passes at ~4.97:1); for the SpeciesDetail pill, use the darker tier-text token rather than the raw tier color for tier 1.

title: axe color-contrast: 139 runtime instances in light theme, traceable to ~4 token-level causes
description: axe-core rule `color-contrast` (impact: serious), 139 violating nodes across all 10 tabs at default (light) theme, deduped by failing color pair: (a) --sr-accent #2D8653 (globals.css:29) used as small text fails by a hair on every light surface — 4.32:1 on #f9fafb (active tab label in TabNav, all 10 tabs), 4.03:1 on #e8f5ee accent-bg (selected segmented/sort buttons, 24x), 4.11–4.33:1 on #f4f4f5/#fafafa (links, 9x); (b) --sr-text-muted #71717A (globals.css:18) on --sr-surface-subtle #f4f4f5 = 4.39:1 — the 66 "Jump to section" nav pills (BirdingStats.tsx:450) and similar chips; (c) --sr-text-disabled #A1A1AA (globals.css:19) used for INFORMATIVE text at 2.33–2.56:1 — result-count announcements ("87 comments" aria-live spans in Checklists/LifeList), empty date-input text (color: var(--sr-text-disabled) at SpeciesDetail.tsx:638 etc.), "267 species" counts — worst offenders; (d) chart/inline labels: hardcoded white 10px % labels on --sr-graph-photo #3B82F6 bars = 3.67:1 (BirdingStats.tsx:1153, 5x) and on --sr-graph-video #8B5CF6 = 4.23:1; --sr-tier-1 #C084FC 1.5rem-bold breeding "Possible" count on white = 2.64:1, below even the 3:1 large-text threshold (BirdingStats.tsx:1613); --sr-accent-border-strong text "Loaded from Settings" on accent-bg = 2.52:1 (ListComparer); Settings date-format sublabels 3.16–3.33:1.
fix: Token-level fixes in globals.css :root — darken --sr-accent to ~#277448 (≥4.5 on #f4f4f5) and --sr-text-muted to ~#65656e; stop using --sr-text-disabled for informative text (counts, date values) — switch those to --sr-text-muted; for chart labels either darken the bar fills the white text sits on or move labels outside the bars; use --sr-tier-1 only for swatches, not text, or pair the tier-1 stat with a darker text token.

title: axe aria-prohibited-attr: aria-label on non-interactive drag-handle <div>s in Tab Layout settings
description: axe-core rule `aria-prohibited-attr` (impact: serious), 9 instances (one per tab row) on the Settings tab. aria-label is prohibited on an element with an implicit generic role, so the "Drag to reorder X tab" name is ignored or inconsistently exposed by AT — and since the handle is a plain div, it is not focusable or operable by keyboard anyway (the sr-only caveat note at Settings.tsx:699 acknowledges mouse-only reorder).
fix: Short term: drop the aria-label (or change the div to aria-hidden="true") so the prohibited attribute is gone and the handle is honestly decorative. Proper fix: make the handle a <button> with that aria-label plus keyboard reorder (ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the row), which would also retire the mouse-only caveat.

title: axe aria-hidden-focus: focusable recharts SVG inside aria-hidden observer-pie wrapper
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 2.4.3 Focus Order A)
description: axe-core rule `aria-hidden-focus` (impact: serious), 1 instance on the Statistics tab. The decorative observers donut is wrapped in <div aria-hidden="true">, but the recharts <PieChart> renders its SVG with tabIndex=0 (recharts accessibilityLayer default), so keyboard users Tab into an element that screen readers cannot perceive — a focus ghost with no announcement.
fix: Pass accessibilityLayer={false} (or tabIndex={-1}) to this PieChart so the hidden decorative chart is also removed from the tab order. Audit the other aria-hidden chart wrappers for the same recharts default.

title: Map popups cannot be dismissed with the keyboard (no close button, no Escape)
description: Every app-rendered map popup passes closeButton={false}, and MapLibre's Popup has no built-in Escape handling (verified: no keydown/Escape in maplibre-gl/src/ui/popup.ts), so the only dismissal is a pointer click on empty map. The Map Explorer in-view list rows open popups by keyboard (good) but never close them: onActivate always sets the locId (MapExplorer.tsx:504-512) — re-activating a row with aria-pressed="true" does not toggle it off, so the pressed state is also a one-way lie. Affected popups: SightingMarkers.tsx:111, HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. A stuck-open popup overlays the map and inserts extra tab stops (eBird links inside it). The AtlasLayer popup (AtlasLayer.tsx:205) is the one that keeps the default close button — proving the styled close button is available.
fix: Either re-enable closeButton (MapLibre renders a real <button aria-label="Close popup">, already themed via .maplibregl-popup-content CSS), or add an Escape keydown handler that clears the selection state, and make in-view list rows toggle (activating the already-selected row calls onSelect(null)). Any one of these resolves it; the row toggle also fixes the aria-pressed semantics.

title: Atlas block popup is only openable by pointer click on the GL fill layer
description: The California atlas block popup (block name, code, and the link to the eBird Atlas portal for that block) opens solely via map.on('click', 'sr-atlas-fill', …) — a canvas hit-test with no DOM focus path. Unlike the sighting pins, hotspots, and targets, there is no keyboard-accessible in-view list for atlas blocks, so the block-details/atlas-portal-link functionality is unavailable without a pointer. The atlas TOGGLE switches themselves are fine (real role="switch" buttons).
fix: Add a capped "Atlas blocks in view" entry path mirroring InViewMarkerList (rows open the same block popup), or at minimum a keyboard-reachable control that opens the block containing the map center. Update ACCESSIBILITY.md's map-markers section accordingly when fixed.

title: WelcomeScreen modal has no focus trap; map fullscreen overlay leaves hidden chrome tabbable
description: WelcomeScreen declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and handles only Escape (line 21) — there is no Tab containment and the app behind it is not inert, so tabbing past "Explore the app first" moves focus into the fully obscured app underneath (the overlay background is opaque var(--sr-bg)); a sighted keyboard user loses the focus indicator entirely while aria-modal simultaneously tells screen readers the background doesn't exist. The map fullscreen mode has the same background-tabbing issue: it is a CSS overlay (panel fixed inset 0, App.tsx:1031-1042) and only body scroll is locked (App.tsx:390-395), so the tab bar and footer remain in the tab order while visually covered. (Not a 2.1.2 trap — focus can always leave — but focus lands on invisible controls.)
fix: Give WelcomeScreen the same Tab-wrap handler HelpDocs uses (HelpDocs.tsx:256-274). For map fullscreen, set inert (or aria-hidden + tabindex management) on the sibling app chrome while active, and consider Escape-to-exit-fullscreen as polish.

title: Map Explorer mobile filter focus trap snapshots focusables once — focus can escape as content changes
description: The mobile filter sidebar trap queries focusable elements once when the overlay opens and captures first/last in the closure (lines 192-196). The sidebar's content is highly dynamic — the Filters accordion expands, the hotspot legend and in-view marker lists appear after a fetch and update on every pan/zoom, Show-all reveals rows. Once elements exist after the stale `last`, Tab from the actual last element is not intercepted and focus walks out of the modal into the backdrop-covered page; elements past the stale `last` are also skipped by the wrap. Escape + focus return (lines 200-203) work correctly. HelpDocs already implements the correct pattern (re-query inside the keydown handler, HelpDocs.tsx:261-263).
fix: Move the querySelectorAll inside handleKeyDown so first/last reflect the live DOM on every Tab press, matching HelpDocs.tsx.

title: In-page jump links scroll the view but never move keyboard focus
description: The Statistics "Jump to section" nav (9 anchors) calls e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and LifeList's "media comments" anchor does the same (LifeList.tsx:505). preventDefault suppresses the browser's native sequential-focus relocation for fragment navigation, and the scroll targets are plain divs without tabindex="-1" (e.g. MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40), so after "jumping" a keyboard user's focus is still on the link at the top — the next Tab continues from the nav and they must traverse every control between anyway. The jump feature is effectively visual-only for keyboard users.
fix: After scrolling, move focus to the destination: give each section container tabindex={-1} and call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }) alongside smoothScrollIntoView (wrap in the existing scroll helper so all jump links inherit it).

title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

title: Bird-name links replace the standard focus ring with only a color change + underline
wcag: 2.4.7 Focus Visible AA (weak indicator; 2.4.13 Focus Appearance fail forward-looking)
description: `.sr-birdname-link:hover, .sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; outline: none; }` — the class rule out-specifies the global `button:focus-visible` outline, so the most common interactive element in the app (every species name in Life List, Breeding Codes, Checklists, Map Explorer, Statistics, comparer rows) shows only a green tint + underline on keyboard focus, identical to the mouse hover style. In a dense table of hundreds of rows this is materially harder to track than the 3px ring used everywhere else, and it weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim of a 'clear green outline' wherever focus lands. The global rule's faint 12% box-shadow still applies but contributes almost nothing.
fix: Split the selector: keep `outline: none` for :hover only, and let :focus-visible keep (or restore) the global outline alongside the color/underline — e.g. `.sr-birdname-link:focus-visible { color: var(--sr-accent); text-decoration: underline; }` with no outline override.

title: Map fullscreen overlay: no Escape exit and focus tabs into content obscured behind the overlay
wcag: 2.4.3 Focus Order A (also 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum, WCAG 2.2 AA)
description: Fullscreen turns the Map Explorer tabpanel into `position: fixed; inset: 0; zIndex: 1200` (App.tsx:1031-1034) with body scroll locked (App.tsx:390-395), but no keydown handler exits it (grep confirms no Escape handler in App.tsx; the only Escape handlers in the app are the sidebar trap, HelpDocs, the combobox, TabNav, WelcomeScreen). The page chrome (tab bar, footer links, other panels' controls) stays in the DOM and in the tab order BEHIND the overlay, so a keyboard user who tabs past the map's controls watches focus vanish under the map — the focus indicator is rendered but fully obscured. Exit is possible only by finding the Exit-fullscreen FAB again. Escape is the universally expected exit for a viewport-takeover, and the obscured-focus walk is disorienting.
fix: While mapFullscreen: add a document keydown listener that exits on Escape (returning focus to the fullscreen toggle), and apply `inert` to the app shell siblings (or trap Tab within the fullscreen panel) so focus cannot land behind the overlay.

title: Help overlay closes without restoring focus to the control that opened it
description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab (re-querying per keydown — the best trap in the codebase), but on close (Escape at line 257 or the Close button) the overlay unmounts with focus inside it and nothing restores focus: App.tsx:1205 is just `onClose={() => setHelpOpen(false)}`. Focus drops to <body>, so a keyboard user who opened Help from the footer Help button, Settings' 'Open help', or the Welcome screen must Tab from the top of the document to get back to where they were. Standard dialog behavior is to return focus to the invoking element.
fix: Capture `document.activeElement` when helpOpen becomes true (or pass an opener ref) and `.focus()` it after the overlay unmounts; same for the Welcome-screen-opened case.

title: One-shot buttons unmount on activation, dropping keyboard focus to <body>
description: Repeated pattern: a focused control disappears when activated, resetting focus to the document body so the keyboard user's next Tab restarts from the top of the page. Locations: 'Show all N' one-shot buttons rendered behind `{!showAll && ...}` — Checklists.tsx:205 (comments) and :718 (checklist rows), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:159, SpeciesDetail.tsx:1347 (species comments); and Settings KeyRow Save/Cancel — Settings.tsx:457 (Cancel) and the post-save `setEditing(false)` at :973 unmount the editing row that contains the focused button. (The toggle-style variants that stay mounted — SpeciesDetail locations/co-occurrence, BirdingStats counties — are fine and are the model to copy.)
fix: Either keep the button mounted as a toggle ('Show fewer'), or on activation move focus explicitly — e.g. focus the first newly revealed row, or for KeyRow focus the Edit button that replaces the editor.

title: Species combobox Escape blurs the input, stranding focus on <body>
description: The Escape branch of the combobox keydown closes the listbox and then deliberately calls `.blur()` on the input: `(e.target as HTMLInputElement).blur()`. Per the ARIA combobox pattern, Escape should close the popup and KEEP focus in the input (a second Escape may clear it). Blurring sends focus to <body>, so a keyboard user dismissing the list loses their place entirely and must Tab back from the top of the page. The blur also exists to suppress the onFocus auto-open (line 481-485 reopens on focus), which compounds the problem: refocusing the input to continue reopens the dropdown whether wanted or not.
fix: Drop the `.blur()` and keep focus in the input; guard the onFocus auto-open with a 'just closed via Escape' flag (or only auto-open on user input/ArrowDown) instead of throwing focus away.

title: Tab key in the collapsed nav dropdown unmounts the focused option before the browser moves focus
description: In TabDropdown, the menu's Tab case calls `close(false)` without preventDefault, intending the browser to move focus onward naturally. But focus lives on a menu option (real DOM focus, line 176/182), and React 18 flushes the discrete keydown update synchronously — the listbox (rendered behind `{open && ...}`, line 265) unmounts and the focused option is removed BEFORE the browser performs the default Tab traversal. Focus falls to <body>, so the default Tab then lands on the first focusable element in the document instead of the control after the trigger. On narrow/mobile widths this dropdown is the app's primary navigation, so Tab-to-leave silently teleports keyboard users to the top of the page. (Escape, by contrast, correctly returns focus to the trigger via close(true).)
fix: On Tab: `e.preventDefault(); close(true)` then let the user Tab from the trigger — or preventDefault and programmatically focus the element after the trigger. Either keeps focus deterministic.

title: Map popups have no close button and never manage focus for the links inside them
description: All five MapLibre popups are rendered with `closeButton={false}` and contain real focusable eBird links: map/HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, map/SightingMarkers.tsx:111, map/TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. When a popup is opened from the keyboard-accessible sidebar lists, focus stays on the sidebar row — the popup's links are only reachable by tabbing through the intervening map chrome, and there is no keyboard affordance to dismiss the popup. Worse, the popup is a single state-driven instance: selecting another row, clicking the map, or panning unmounts it, and if a link inside had focus, focus is dropped to <body>. (The sidebar rows carry equivalent aria-labeled eBird links, which keeps this from being serious — the popup is a redundant path — but the focus drop on unmount is still a real degradation.)
fix: When a popup opens from a sidebar row, optionally move focus to the popup's first link and return it to the row on close; at minimum, before unmounting a popup check if document.activeElement is inside it and restore focus to the owning row/control. Consider closeButton for parity.

title: Sortable column headers are focusable <th> with no interactive role
description: Sortable headers are <th tabIndex={0} onClick onKeyDown> with aria-sort (LifeListTable.tsx:188-250, BreedingCodeTable.tsx:120-160). aria-sort updates correctly, but the element exposes role columnheader only — nothing announces it as an activatable control, so a screen-reader user tabbing onto "Entries" or "NB" hears a plain column header and has no cue that Enter/Space re-sorts. The BreedingCodeTable code headers additionally expose only the terse code (e.g. "NB") as the name, with the expansion in title only.
fix: Put a real <button> inside each sortable <th> (th keeps aria-sort, button carries the label e.g. "Sort by Entries"); for breeding-code columns give the button an aria-label with the code's full label.

title: Collapsed dropdown nav orphans every tabpanel (dangling aria-labelledby, no tablist)
description: All panels in App.tsx use aria-labelledby="tab-{id}" (e.g. App.tsx:590). In the collapsed TabDropdown mode the id="tab-{id}" elements exist only on the listbox options while the menu is open (TabNav.tsx:298) — with the menu closed (the normal state) the visible role="tabpanel" references a nonexistent id and there is no tablist/tab anywhere in the tree, so the tab/tabpanel relationship ACCESSIBILITY.md claims ("Tabs and their panels are linked with the correct tab/tabpanel roles") is broken precisely for the zoom/narrow-viewport users who get the dropdown. The dropdown also replaces tab semantics with listbox semantics, leaving orphaned tabpanels.
fix: Give panels a stable label that doesn't depend on the bar variant — e.g. aria-label={TAB_LABELS[id]} on each panel (or keep aria-labelledby but render persistent visually-hidden label elements), and use distinct ids for dropdown options.

title: Entire Weather tabpanel is an aria-live aria-atomic region
description: The whole weather panel carries aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" (App.tsx:591-592). With aria-atomic, ANY mutation — the button flipping to "Looking up…", Copy → "Copied!", the tide box changing state — re-announces the entire panel content (label, help text, full weather <pre>, tide section). The nested role="alert" (:720) and role="status" elements (:837-845) inside the live region then announce the same changes a second time. Screen-reader users get long duplicate read-outs after every interaction on the default tab.
fix: Remove aria-live/aria-atomic from the tabpanel; rely on the existing scoped role="alert"/role="status" children, and add a small persistent polite region for "Weather copied to clipboard" if needed.

title: Update-check outcomes are not reliably announced ('available' and 'error' not at all)
description: The footer update checker swaps conditionally-rendered spans per state. 'checking' (:1148), 'up-to-date' (:1154) and 'downloading' (:1180) have aria-live="polite" but each span MOUNTS already containing its text — newly-inserted live regions with initial content are inconsistently announced by AT. The two states that matter most, 'available' (:1156-1178, with its Install update button) and 'error' (:1190), have no live semantics at all, so a screen-reader user who activates "Check For Updates" may hear nothing whatsoever.
fix: Render ONE persistent <span aria-live="polite"> in the footer and change its text content across all update states, instead of mounting/unmounting per-state spans.

title: Map Explorer async error messages are silent to assistive tech
description: The hotspot search error (:1006-1011) and media-targets search error (:1227-1232) render as plain styled divs after an async failure — no role="alert" or aria-live, so a screen-reader user who pressed "Find Hotspots"/"Find Recent Sightings" gets no feedback that the request failed (the role="status" loading chip just disappears). Other error paths in the app do this correctly (ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, App.tsx:720, DropZone.tsx:132).
fix: Add role="alert" to both error divs (matching ChecklistComparer's pattern).

title: role="radio" groups in Settings have no arrow-key behavior or roving tabindex
description: Theme (:119-128), Text size (:519-525), and Date format (:586-591) use role="radiogroup"/role="radio" with aria-checked, but every radio is a tabIndex={0} button and arrow keys do nothing. The radio role contract tells SR users "radio button, 1 of 3 — use arrow keys"; pressing arrows is a no-op, and Tab walks through each radio as a separate stop. Operable but misleading — the role advertises an interaction model the widget doesn't implement.
fix: Either implement the radiogroup pattern (roving tabindex + ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down + Home/End), or swap to plain buttons with aria-pressed (matching SortSeg) which matches the actual Tab-based interaction.

title: Marker-kind sr-only labels are nested inside aria-hidden and never reach AT
description: In InViewMarkerList — the documented keyboard/SR alternative to the GL map pins — the colored kind dot is CONTAINING {getDotLabel(item)}. aria-hidden removes the entire subtree from the accessibility tree, including the sr-only text, so the hotspot kind / recency information conveyed by dot color is announced to no one. ACCESSIBILITY.md explicitly claims "map recency dots — carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader"; the code makes that claim false.
fix: Move the sr-only label outside the aria-hidden dot span: keep the dot aria-hidden, and render the sr-only kind label as a sibling inside the row button.

title: ChecklistBadges convey present/absent state via aria-label on generic spans; group unnamed
description: Each Badge is a role-less <span aria-label={presentTitle|absentTitle}>. ARIA prohibits naming on the generic role, and screen readers inconsistently honor aria-label on plain spans in browse mode — so SR users may hear only the visible "Photo Audio Video Breeding Weather Tide" text with the present/absent state (the badge's entire point) dropped. The wrapping role="group" (:53) also has no accessible name. The tests assert the aria-labels exist but can't catch the exposure problem.
fix: Add role="img" to the Badge span (making the aria-label valid and reliably announced), and aria-label="Checklist contents" on the role="group" container.

title: No h1, most views have no headings, and heading levels are inconsistent across tabs
description: The app title "SnowRaven" is styled <span>s in a <div> (App.tsx:570-580) — no h1 and no banner landmark. Settings, Life List, Species Detail, and Map Explorer contain no heading elements at all (section titles like "Appearance"/"Map Overlays" are styled divs), so SR heading navigation lands on nothing in four major views. Where headings do exist they are inconsistent: ListComparer.tsx:184 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:340 use h1 inside tab content while Checklists.tsx:522, BirdingStats.tsx:424 and NamedBirds.tsx:128 use h2; SetupRequired.tsx:31 (the empty state of 8 tabs) styles its title as a div. Additionally the main nav loses its landmark: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides the navigation role, and in dropdown mode there is no nav element at all.
fix: Make the app title an h1 inside a <header>; give every tab view an h2 and section cards h3 (Settings/LifeList/SpeciesDetail/MapExplorer sidebar sections); make SetupRequired's title an h2; demote the comparer h1s to h2.

title: Disclosed chart-bar-label exception verified — but it understates the dark-theme failures (down to 1.29:1) and a working fix already exists in-code
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md's known exception ('a few dense data-visualization labels (percentage figures printed inside saturated chart bars) do not yet meet AA in every case') is accurate in direction but materially understates scope. Computed: LIGHT — white on --sr-graph-audio 2.15:1 (protocol bar), white on --sr-chart-slate 2.56:1, white on --sr-graph-photo 3.68:1, white on --sr-graph-video 4.23:1. DARK — --sr-text on --sr-chart-blue-light 1.29:1 (comment/species-notes bars, BirdingStats.tsx:1384/1405), white on graph-audio 1.44:1, white on --sr-accent 1.92:1 (hardcoded '#fff' at protocol bar :1181), white on graph-photo 2.54:1, white on chart-slate 2.56:1, --sr-text on chart-slate 2.33:1 (:1361), white on chart-blue-dark 3.68:1 (:1125). In dark mode it is most in-bar labels, not 'a few'. Notably, line 1358 already uses var(--sr-on-accent) which passes in BOTH themes (4.52/7.75) — the failures are the literal '#fff' and var(--sr-text) usages that don't adapt.
fix: Replace literal '#fff' bar-label colors with per-fill adaptive tokens (the existing --sr-on-accent pattern), or render the percentage outside/beside the segment when the segment color can't carry AA text; then tighten the ACCESSIBILITY.md wording to match whatever remains.

title: Dark theme: map pin tokens are lightened 'for dark backgrounds' but draw on the always-light Positron basemap (1.69–2.25:1)
description: There is no dark basemap variant (lib/mapStyle.ts tunes Positron only; no theme branch), yet the dark-theme --sr-map-* tokens lighten the pin colors: visited/heat pins #34D399 vs Positron land (~#F2F0EB) = 1.69:1, personal #E0A060 = 1.97:1, unvisited #7BA7C9 = 2.25:1 (light theme passes: 3.66–3.97:1). The GL circle/teardrop sprites read these tokens at runtime (map/SightingMarkers.tsx:80, lib/mapPins.ts, HotspotMarkers sprites), so switching the app to dark mode makes the primary map markers fainter against the unchanged light tiles. White glyphs inside the dark-theme teardrops also drop below 3:1 (star on #E0A060 = 2.24:1, dots on #7BA7C9 = 2.56:1). Mitigation: the sidebar in-view lists duplicate marker info, which keeps this from serious.
fix: Anchor the on-map pin tokens to the basemap, not the app theme (keep the light-theme values in dark mode, or add a dark halo/outline to the GL sprites); keep the lightened values only for sidebar legend dots that actually sit on dark surfaces.

title: Light theme: accent-colored text marginally fails on tinted/page backgrounds (4.03–4.32:1)
description: Light --sr-accent #2D8653 passes on white surfaces (4.52:1) but fails where it is used on anything tinted: on --sr-accent-bg = 4.03:1 — the app-wide active-state pattern (ghost buttons, active filter pills, the tab dropdown's selected option TabNav.tsx:309-314, SpeciesPanel count badge :44-45; background:'var(--sr-accent-bg)' + accent text appears in 14 files); on --sr-bg = 4.32:1 — the active tab label (tab bar sits directly on the page background, App.tsx:583) and the footer 'Up to date' status (App.tsx:1154); on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.11:1. Dark theme passes everywhere (7.75–10.35:1).
fix: In light theme use --sr-accent-strong (#1A5C38; 7.12:1 on accent-bg, ~6.7:1 on bg) for accent-as-TEXT on tinted/page backgrounds, keeping --sr-accent for fills, borders and focus rings; or darken light --sr-accent to ~#27764A so it clears 4.5:1 on --sr-accent-bg.

title: Light theme: error text on error background is just below AA (4.41:1)
description: --sr-error #DC2626 on --sr-error-bg #FEF2F2 computes to 4.41:1 — marginally under 4.5:1 — and this pair styles every error banner and the 'negative' filter pill state: Checklists.tsx:236/488, LifeList.tsx:108/384, BreedingCodeList.tsx:196, Settings.tsx:304/480, ChecklistComparer.tsx:374, NamedBirds.tsx:108, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:186, SpeciesDetail.tsx:430, DropZone.tsx error text. Dark theme passes (7.07:1). Error on plain surface also passes (4.83:1), so only the tinted-banner pair needs a nudge.
fix: Darken light --sr-error slightly (e.g. #D31F1F ≈ 4.8:1 on #FEF2F2) or introduce an --sr-error-text token used on --sr-error-bg; one token edit in globals.css fixes all listed locations.

title: Light theme: muted text on tinted surfaces falls just under AA (4.27–4.40:1)
description: --sr-text-muted #71717A passes on white (4.83:1) but not on the tinted surfaces it is commonly paired with in light theme: on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.40:1 (inactive segmented-control labels in MapSidebarUI SegControl, the basemap switcher buttons in globals.css:246, the missing-media badges in the target popup TargetMarkers.tsx:92, numerous chips); on --sr-quote-bg = 4.27:1 (Named Birds comment block); on --sr-accent-bg = 4.31:1 (secondary text inside selected rows, e.g. the location line of a selected Nearest Targets row, MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317). Dark theme passes all three (5.27–5.82:1).
fix: Darken light --sr-text-muted to ~#6B6B74 (≈4.6:1 on #F4F4F5) — a single token change; verify it still reads as 'muted' next to --sr-text.

title: ToggleSwitch off-state track is nearly invisible in light theme (1.48:1)
description: The off-state track uses --sr-gray-400 (#D4D4D8): 1.48:1 against the white button surface AND 1.48:1 against the white knob, so the knob position — the visual state indicator of every 'merge subspecies' / 'show spuh' / 'hide weather' switch — is barely discernible in light theme (the on state passes: accent track 4.52:1 vs surface). Dark theme: track vs surface 2.29:1 (also <3:1) though knob-vs-track passes (7.73:1). aria-checked is correct for AT, but the sighted off/on distinction fails non-text contrast.
fix: Darken the light off-track (e.g. #8E8E96 ≈ 3.1:1 on white and vs the white knob) and lighten the dark off-track (e.g. #6E6E78), or add a 1px --sr-border-medium-darkened outline to the track and knob.

title: Form-control borders are far below non-text contrast (1.19–1.34:1)
description: --sr-border (#E4E4E7 light / #27272A dark) is the only boundary cue on text inputs, selects, date inputs and unselected pills throughout the app (SELECT_STYLE here; the same '1px/1.5px solid var(--sr-border)' pattern on inputs in MapExplorer, Checklists, LifeList, Settings, SpeciesDetail). Computed: 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark vs surface, 1.21:1 / 1.34:1 vs page bg; even --sr-border-medium is 1.73:1 light / 1.70:1 dark. Inputs whose extent is identified only by this border fail 1.4.11; the focus ring fixes it only once focused.
fix: Introduce an --sr-border-input token at ≥3:1 vs surface (≈#949499 light, ≈#5F5F66 dark) for form-control boundaries, or give inputs a contrasting filled background (--sr-surface-subtle is itself only 1.07:1 vs surface, so the border route is simpler).

title: Hardcoded milestone-chip and rank-icon colors below AA (2.76–4.16:1), bypassing the token system
description: The Firsts & Milestones chips hardcode hex colors (also violating the project's tokens-only rule): the tier-1 date link #5EA07C on #E8F5EE = 2.76:1 (10px text), tier-1 number #2D8653 on #E8F5EE = 4.03:1, tier-2 date #3E7A56 on #D8EDE4 = 4.16:1 (tier-3/4 pass: 4.92–6.37:1). These values are identical in both themes since the chips don't adapt. Separately, RankIcon (statsPrimitives.tsx:97-98) prints white 10px-bold rank numbers on hardcoded #3B82F6 = 3.68:1 (the #2D8653 circle squeaks by at 4.52:1).
fix: Move the milestone palette into --sr-* tokens and darken the failing fg values (date ≥ #43755C on #E8F5EE; num → --sr-accent-strong); for RankIcon use --sr-chart-blue-dark (#1D4ED8, 6.70:1 under white) as the square fill.

title: 'Personal Location' popup badge fails in light theme (2.90:1)
description: The hotspot popup's 'Personal Location' badge sets --sr-map-personal (#C9842A) text on --sr-is-target-bg (#FFF7ED): 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 (dark passes, 8.38:1). The pin color token was designed as a map fill, not a text color.
fix: Use --sr-is-target-text (#C2410C, 4.88:1 on that bg) or --sr-warning for the badge text in light theme.

title: DropZone error state's border and icon are nearly invisible (1.74–1.90:1)
description: In the error state the drop zone's border and upload icon switch to --sr-error-muted (#FCA5A5 light): 1.74:1 against the --sr-error-bg fill and 1.90:1 against the surrounding surface, so the state-change boundary/icon fails non-text contrast (dark: icon vs surface 2.74:1; vs error-bg 3.02:1 passes). The role=alert error text is present, but it itself is the marginal 4.41:1 light error-on-error-bg pair reported separately.
fix: Use --sr-error (#DC2626) for the error-state border and icon — 4.41:1 vs error-bg and 4.83:1 vs surface, comfortably over the 3:1 non-text bar.

title: ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim is broader than the computed reality
description: The published statement says text, buttons, links, map popups and form controls 'meet the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standard (4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes', with chart-bar labels as the only known exception. Computed counterexamples outside that exception: light-theme active pills/links on tinted backgrounds 4.03–4.41:1 (accent-on-accent-bg, error-on-error-bg, active tab on page bg), --sr-text-disabled used on content at 2.29–2.56:1, dark-theme target chips at 1.52–1.92:1, dark-theme breeding pills at 1.97–2.94:1, and form-control borders at 1.19–1.27:1 (non-text). The repo treats this file as a published statement whose claims must be true; today it overstates. (Verified-true parts: the tier-1 badge example, the recency-dot hidden labels, the text-footer/sci-name token fixes, focus-ring contrast, and the dark-mode popup theming.)
fix: Either fix the token-level failures in this report (most are 1-line token edits) and keep the claim, or temporarily widen the known-exceptions paragraph to honestly cover active-state tints in light theme and chip/pill labels in dark theme.

title: Media count badges in checklist comparer use aria-label on a generic <span> — info silently lost to screen readers
description: MediaIcons renders per-species photo/audio/video presence as lucide SVG icons inside a plain <span aria-label={`${n} ${label}`}>. ARIA prohibits naming on role=generic, so most browser/SR pairs ignore the aria-label, and the SVGs themselves have no text alternative — the media information (which types exist and counts) is conveyed to sighted users only. The same file's Checklists tab equivalent (Checklists.tsx:276 Badge) does this correctly with role="img", and ChecklistBadges.tsx is correct too — this one component missed the pattern.
fix: Add role="img" to the span (matching the Badge pattern in Checklists.tsx:276) so the aria-label is exposed: <span role="img" aria-label={`${n} ${label}`} ...>.

title: Repeated "↗" checklist links named only by the arrow glyph
wcag: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) A / 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA
description: Three Statistics sections render external eBird checklist links whose only content is the character "↗" with title="Open checklist": the effort superlative cards (line 1332), single-checklist-bird chips (line 1564), and one-and-done bird chips (line 1589). The accessible name is computed from content, so every one of these (potentially dozens in the chip lists) is announced as "north east arrow, link" or skipped entirely depending on SR symbol verbosity — identical and non-descriptive. title only provides a description, not the name, when content exists.
fix: Add aria-label, e.g. aria-label={`Open eBird checklist ${bird.submissionId} for ${bird.name} (opens in a new tab)`}, mirroring NamedBirdRow.tsx:94 which already does this correctly, and mark the glyph aria-hidden.

title: Missing-media type icons in Media Targets popup and marker chips have no text alternative anywhere
description: The whole point of a media target is which media types (photo/audio/video) the user is missing, but that information is conveyed exclusively by unnamed inline SVGs: in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97, bare <svg> per missing type, no aria-hidden, no label), in the on-map chip labels (TargetMarkers.tsx:62, MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the keyboard-accessible "Nearest Targets" sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:~1315-1318) show only name/location/distance — they omit missing types entirely. A screen-reader user can find a target but never learn which media it is missing. This also weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that icon-only information "carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader."
fix: In the popup, give each type span role="img" aria-label={`Missing ${t.toLowerCase()}`} (or append sr-only text) and aria-hidden the SVGs; add the missing types as text (visible or sr-only) to the Nearest Targets sidebar rows so the keyboard/SR path carries the full information.

title: DOM map markers (Species Detail / Named Birds pins, target chips, Statistics rank pins) are unnamed, role-less click targets invisible to AT
wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content A / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md documents sidebar-list alternatives for the Map Explorer's GPU canvas markers, but the DOM <Marker> maps have no equivalent treatment: SightingsMap.tsx:55-58 renders each pin as a clickable <div> containing an innerHTML SVG with no role, name, or tabindex; TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 does the same for target chips; BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 for the Statistics RankIcon pins (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101, an unnamed SVG). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or activate any of these markers or reach their popups. Impact is moderated because equivalent data exists in adjacent text on most surfaces (Named Birds rows list every sighting date/location/checklist; Species Detail has Top Locations and per-sighting lists; Statistics has top-location tables), but the popup-only details (e.g. per-coordinate date groupings) have no named path.
fix: Make the Marker child a real button: role="button", tabIndex=0, aria-label like `${locName ?? coordinate}, ${sightings.length} sightings` with Enter/Space handling — or explicitly scope the ACCESSIBILITY.md marker claim and guarantee a text equivalent exists beside every DOM-marker map.

title: Placeholder-only (or format-only) accessible names on text inputs; Map Explorer From/To dates are indistinguishable
wcag: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA / 1.3.1 Info and Relationships A
description: Several inputs have no label or aria-label, so the accessible name falls back to the placeholder. Worst case: the Map Explorer date-range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862,864) both have placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD" — a SR user hears the format string twice with nothing distinguishing From vs To (the visible "Date Range" SidebarLabel is not programmatically associated). Same pattern: MapExplorer.tsx:84 (place search), 689/691 (Latitude/Longitude), 1182 (target species search); Settings.tsx:1216/1228/1240 map-default inputs, whose visible "Latitude"/"Longitude"/"Radius (mi)" labels are unassociated <div>s so the computed name is "e.g. 37.8275"; SpeciesDetail.tsx:1268 and MediaCommentsSection.tsx:70 comment filters (placeholder is at least descriptive there, but disappears once text is typed for sighted users). Contrast: Checklists.tsx:655/663 date inputs do it right with aria-label="From date"/"To date".
fix: Add aria-label to each (e.g. "From date (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "To date (YYYY-MM-DD)", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Search by place name"), or associate the existing visible labels via htmlFor/id.

title: Placeholder is the only label on search/filter, coordinate, and API-key text inputs
description: These text inputs have no label or aria-label; their only identification is the placeholder, which disappears as soon as the user types (and browsers' placeholder→accessible-name fallback is a last resort, not a reliable label). Locations: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-70 ('Filter media comments…'); Checklists.tsx:161-165 (shared CommentSearchBox, placeholders 'Filter checklist comments…' / 'Filter species comments…' at :544/:555); SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1268 ('Filter comments…'); MapExplorer.tsx:82-84 ('Search by place name'), :689/:691 (Latitude/Longitude number inputs — after entry a sighted user sees two bare numbers with nothing saying which is which), :1182-1184 ('Search species…'); Settings.tsx:424-428 (API key entry, 'Paste your API key' — the row label at :352 is an unassociated <div>). Impact is worst for low-vision and cognitive users mid-entry, and for the lat/lng pair where the only differentiator vanishes.
fix: Add aria-label to each input (e.g. aria-label="Filter media comments", aria-label="Latitude", aria-label="eBird API key") while keeping the placeholder as a hint; for the Map Explorer lat/lng pair, prefer small visible labels like the Settings map-defaults section already has.

title: Atlas block popups are pointer-only — no keyboard route to open them
description: Atlas block info popups open exclusively via a MapLibre map.on('click','sr-atlas-fill') handler on the GL fill layer (AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132). There is no sidebar list, search, or other focusable path to a block, so the popup's content — block name, the eBird atlas portal link, and 'Highest breeding code … N of your breeding records in this block' — is unreachable without a pointer. The breeding data shown in the popup is not surfaced anywhere else in the app (the sidebar legend only explains tier colors). The popup JSX itself is fine (escaped, keeps the default labeled close button), but keyboard users can never open it.
fix: When shading is on, add a focusable 'Shaded blocks in view' sidebar list (mirroring InViewMarkerList — blocksInBounds already provides viewport-scoped blocks and breedingByBlock the per-block data) whose rows open the same popup; or expose a block search/jump input. Cap + hint like the other lists.

title: Map sidebar filter inputs rely on placeholders for their accessible names; date inputs are named 'YYYY-MM-DD'
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions A)
description: The Map Explorer sidebar inputs have no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby — the SidebarLabel headings are unassociated styled divs. Accessible names therefore fall back to placeholders: the two Date Range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865) both compute to the meaningless, identical name "YYYY-MM-DD" (a screen-reader user cannot tell From from To, or that they are date filters at all); Latitude/Longitude (:689-692), "Search by place name" (:86), and "Search species…" (:1182) are intelligible but vanish once a value is typed. The adjacent Search button (:90-103) has only a title attribute for its name.
fix: Add aria-label="Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)" (and aria-labels echoing the other placeholders), or give SidebarLabel an id and reference it via aria-labelledby plus a per-field qualifier. Give the search icon button aria-label="Search". (Flagging here because these gate the map experience; may overlap with a forms-dimension audit.)

title: Map chrome text inherits MapLibre's fixed `font: 12px/20px Helvetica` — does not scale with the in-app Text Size control
description:
maplibre-gl.css (imported at SnowMap.tsx:7) sets `.maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,…}`. The app's `.maplibregl-popup-content` override in globals.css:568 themes colors but sets no font-size or family, so any map-rendered text without an explicit rem size stays at a hard 12px Helvetica regardless of the Text Size setting. Affected: (1) the AtlasLayer block popup title — `
{sel.name}
` at AtlasLayer.tsx:213 and the linked variant at :208-211 have no fontSize; (2) the attribution credits on every map (SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}` — provider links render at fixed 12px when expanded); (3) the AtlasLayer popup's default close button (it is the only popup that doesn't pass `closeButton={false}`, so users get maplibre's small fixed-size '×' — also a WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size concern). This matters more here than in a typical web app: ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 states the Text Size control is "especially useful in the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own", so on desktop this text is genuinely un-resizable. All other popups (SightingMarkers, HotspotMarkers, TargetMarkers, SightingsMap, the BirdingStats geo popup) set explicit rem sizes and are fine.
fix: In globals.css extend the existing popup override: `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`; give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize; pass `closeButton={false}` on the AtlasLayer popup for consistency with the other four popups (its onClose path already exists).

title: Fixed-pixel text geometry in Statistics overlaps or clips at 200% text scale (pattern, multiple locations)
wcag: 1.4.4 Resize Text AA (clipping cases also 1.4.12 Text Spacing AA)
description: One repeating pattern: rem-sized text placed in fixed-pixel boxes that don't grow with the text. (1) BarRow (statsPrimitives.tsx:59-75): label column `width: labelWidth, flexShrink: 0` and value column `width: pctOf ? 68 : 40`, no overflow handling — at 200% scale, labels ("Jan" at labelWidth=28: BirdingStats.tsx:754,794,829; "SnowRaven weather" at 120: BirdingStats.tsx:1425-1429; MediaStatsSections.tsx:180-182,294) and values like "1,234 (56%)" are ~2× wider than their boxes and overlap the adjacent bar graphic. (2) Stacked-bar % labels inside fixed-height `overflow: hidden` segments — BirdingStats.tsx:1122-1133 and 1173-1185 (height 32, fits 200%) but the protocol sub-bars at 1151-1158 are `height: 20` with 0.625rem labels: at 200% the 20px glyphs (30px line box) clip vertically; same construction in the media bars at 1356, 1380, 1401. (3) Hard-ellipsized name columns `width: 100`/`width: 96` + nowrap+hidden (BirdingStats.tsx:953, 984, 1028, 1057) — county/species names truncate to a few characters at 200% with only a mouse-only `title` as recovery. (4) Donut center captions absolutely centered in fixed 120/132px charts — BirdingStats.tsx:764-769, 804-807 and MediaStatsSections.tsx:58-61 — at 200% the caption (e.g. "September" ≈140px wide, or a 1.25rem count) spills across the donut ring on both sides. Screen-reader users are unaffected (the role="img" aria-labels carry the data); this degrades the visual rendering for sighted low-vision users at 150-200%.
fix: Convert the fixed widths to rem (e.g. labelWidth 28→'2.5rem', value column '4.5rem') or `minWidth` + `flex-basis`; change the sub-bar `height: 20` to `minHeight: 20` (the % label centers itself, the bar just grows); for the donut captions either size the chart in rem or cap centerValue/centerLabel with a clamp().

title: List Comparer summary bars and result panels don't reflow at 320px — labels truncate to identical text
description: Both comparer results screens use rigid column counts with no narrow-width collapse. The five-cell summary (`gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 1fr)'` — ResultsView.tsx:111 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:281) gives each cell ~58px at 320px; the 0.625rem uppercase labels are `whiteSpace: nowrap; overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis` (ResultsView.tsx:165-173, ChecklistComparer.tsx:478), so "Checklist A" and "Checklist B" (and "<name> total" pairs) ellipsize to identical strings — the numbers become indistinguishable at that width. Below them, ResultsView.tsx:129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` species panels and ChecklistComparer.tsx:310 `1fr 1fr` A-only/B-only panels never stack, leaving ~90-140px columns where species names wrap to 4+ lines. Nothing scrolls two-dimensionally and the panel headers repeat the counts, so it is degraded rather than lost — but the summary labels' ambiguity is a concrete information loss at 320px.
fix: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` for the stat bars (cells wrap to two rows on narrow screens), and collapse the panel grids to one column under 640px (reuse the `.sr-two-col` media-query pattern from globals.css:601).

title: 'Nearest Targets' list is not scoped to the map view and does not update on pan/zoom, contrary to the statement
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md says the Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list 'works the same way' as the in-view lists and then asserts 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom (very dense views are capped, with a "zoom in to narrow the list" hint).' The keyboard path itself is real (each row has a focusable, aria-labelled locate button at lines 1320-1333 that opens the same popup and pans). But `nearest10` (lines 453-461) is computed as the 10 closest pins to the SEARCH CENTER lat/lng inputs — it ignores `mapBounds`, never reacts to panning or zooming, and has no over-cap hint. Only the 'Sightings in view' and 'Hotspots in view' lists (markersInView + mapBounds, cap 200, MapSidebarUI.tsx:118-121) match the published description. A screen-reader user following the statement would expect the targets keyboard list to track the viewport; it doesn't.
fix: Either scope the targets list with markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) like the other two lists, or correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the 10 nearest to the search center.

title: Tab Layout reordering is mouse/touch-only with no keyboard alternative — the statement's keyboard section discloses no exceptions
wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (also WCAG 2.2 2.5.7 Dragging Movements AA)
description: Settings → Tab Layout reorders tabs exclusively via HTML5 drag-and-drop on the <li> rows; the 'drag handle' is a non-focusable plain <div> carrying an aria-label (which is also invalid ARIA on a generic div — it won't be announced), and there is no keyboard mechanism (no move-up/move-down buttons, no arrow-key handling). The app itself admits this in an sr-only note at Settings.tsx:699 ('Keyboard reordering is not supported in this version'), and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'Nearly all of SnowRaven is reachable and operable with the keyboard alone' hedge technically covers it — but the Keyboard Navigation section enumerates zero exceptions, so a reader has no way to learn this feature is keyboard-inaccessible. Show/hide toggles are keyboard-accessible; ordering is not achievable at all without a pointer, which is a hard 2.1.1 failure for that function (and a 2.5.7 Dragging Movements failure under WCAG 2.2).
fix: Add keyboard reordering (focusable handle button with ArrowUp/ArrowDown + aria-live position announcements, or per-row Move up/Move down buttons), and until then name this exception explicitly in ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard section.

title: Closing the Help overlay drops focus to <body> instead of returning to the Help button
description: HelpDocs correctly focuses its Close button on open and traps Tab, but onClose (Close button or Escape) simply unmounts the overlay (App.tsx:1203-1205 just sets helpOpen false) — focus falls to document.body and the keyboard user restarts from the top of the page. The Map Explorer filter sidebar (filtersButtonRef refocus) and the TabNav dropdown (close(true)) both restore focus correctly; HelpDocs is the inconsistent one. It can be opened from three places (footer, Welcome screen, Settings), so the opener should be remembered.
fix: Capture document.activeElement when the overlay mounts and restore focus to it in a cleanup effect (covers all three openers without prop plumbing).

title: DropZone inline `outline: 'none'` defeats the global keyboard focus ring
description: The DropZone (role="button", tabIndex=0 — keyboard activation itself works) sets outline: 'none' in its inline style. Inline styles override the stylesheet's [role="button"]:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sr-accent) } rule (globals.css:546-551, no !important), leaving only the rule's faint 12%-alpha box-shadow glow as the focus indicator; the border/background highlight is driven by mouse-only isHovered state. Keyboard users on the List Comparer get an almost invisible cue on the primary upload control. (Reported here because it directly degrades keyboard operation of an otherwise-correct widget; full focus-visible sweep belongs to that dimension.)
fix: Delete the inline outline: 'none' (the global :focus-visible ring only shows for keyboard focus, so the mouse aesthetics are unaffected), or mirror the isDragging accent border on :focus-visible.

title: WCAG 2.2 deltas: 14×14 favicon link targets and sticky-header focus obscuring
description: Forward-looking 2.2 items. (a) Target size: the eBird / Birds of the World favicon links rendered beside nearly every bird name are 14×14px, placed directly adjacent to each other — below the 24×24 minimum with no qualifying spacing exception; they are the most frequently repeated small target in the app. The Species Detail combobox chevron (SpeciesDetail.tsx:521, ~16px <span>) is also undersized but pointer-redundant. Most other small controls measured are compliant (close 26×26, eye 28×28, locate 26×26, FABs 36×36). (b) 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: LifeListTable's sticky header row (position: sticky, top: 0 — LifeListTable.tsx:182-187) can fully cover row links (BirdName, ML catalog) when Shift+Tab scrolls a focused element up under it; same risk for BreedingCodeTable's sticky first column (line 128).
fix: Give the favicon anchors padding to reach a ≥24×24 hit area (visual size can stay 14px). For sticky tables, add scroll-padding-top equal to the header height on the scroll container so focused elements land below the sticky header.

title: Tablist lacks Home/End keys (APG completeness)
wcag: 2.1.1 Keyboard A (advisory — APG tabs pattern; no AA failure)
description: The desktop tab bar implements roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight + wrap (TabNav.tsx:109-123) but not Home/End to jump to the first/last tab, which the WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern recommends (the collapsed dropdown DOES implement Home/End at lines 197-204, so the two modes are inconsistent). With 10+ tabs this is several extra keystrokes, not a barrier — forward-looking polish only.
fix: Add Home → items[0] and End → items[items.length-1] cases to the tablist onKeyDown, mirroring the dropdown's handling.

title: Map Explorer Filters accordion button lacks aria-expanded
description: The collapsible filter panel toggle in the sightings sidebar (button at :836, panel collapsed via max-height 0) exposes no expanded/collapsed state — the only cue is the rotated chevron. Every other disclosure in the app does carry aria-expanded (NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76/:440, TabNav.tsx:234).
fix: Add aria-expanded={filterOpen} (and optionally aria-controls) to the Filters button.

title: Comment-count live regions announce on every keystroke
description: CommentSearchBox's match count (N comments, used by both the Checklist Comments and Species Comments sections) recomputes from the filter input on every keystroke, so a screen reader queues an "N comments" announcement per character typed, competing with character echo. The count announcement itself is good 4.1.3 practice — it just needs to settle.
fix: Debounce the text feeding the live region (~400-500 ms after typing pauses) while leaving the visible count immediate.

title: Comparison-mode switch uses tablist/tab roles without panels or arrow-key support
description: The Life Lists / Checklists mode switch is role="tablist" + role="tab" aria-selected, but there is no aria-controls, no role="tabpanel" for the swapped content, no roving tabindex, and no arrow-key handling — SR users are told they're in a tab widget whose conventions (arrows move, panel follows) don't hold. Inside the app shell's real tab system, this also nests tab semantics within a tabpanel.
fix: Either complete the pattern (ids + aria-controls + tabpanel + roving tabindex + arrows) or simplify to a role="group" of aria-pressed buttons like SortSeg.

title: TabDropdown listbox misuses aria-activedescendant and trigger lacks aria-controls
description: The dropdown menu manages focus by moving DOM focus to the option buttons (roving), yet the listbox container also sets aria-activedescendant — on an element that itself never receives focus (no tabindex), where the attribute has no effect, and pointing at the SELECTED tab rather than the focused option. All options are also tabIndex={0} (the pattern expects -1 with the container or roving single stop), and the trigger (:233) has aria-haspopup/aria-expanded but no aria-controls referencing the listbox. Functionally usable (DOM focus carries the announcements) but the ARIA contradicts the actual focus model.
fix: Remove aria-activedescendant (DOM focus already tracks the active option), set option tabIndex={-1}, give the listbox an id, and add aria-controls to the trigger.

title: Species selector chevron is a click-only unnamed <span>
description: The open/close chevron beside the species combobox input is a <span onClick> with no role, no accessible name, and no keyboard access. The function is redundantly available (focusing the input opens the list, Escape closes), so impact is low, but it's an interactive element invisible to AT and unreachable by keyboard.
fix: Either mark it decorative (aria-hidden, remove onClick — the input already toggles) or make it a real button with aria-label="Toggle species list" and tabIndex={-1}.

title: role="status" loading indicators mount already containing their text (announcement unreliable)
description: Loading/status chips are conditionally rendered elements that carry role="status" AND their message in the same insertion: TabLoading (App.tsx:125), tide states (App.tsx:837-845), MapExplorer loading chip (:1437), BirdingStats (:464, :883), AtlasLayer (:230), WeatherTidePanel (:165-235). Live regions must exist before their content changes; regions inserted with initial text are announced by some AT/browser combos and skipped by others, so loading/unavailable states are inconsistently conveyed. Pattern issue — reported once for all locations.
